label: Population growth
question: Which country has a higher population growth rate?
definition: The annual change in the resident population, expressed as an exponential growth rate. Includes the combined effects of births, deaths, and migration. Negative values mean the population shrank.

label: Birth rate
question: Which country has more births per person?
definition: Live births during the year per 1,000 residents, using the midyear population. Unlike fertility per woman, this rate also reflects the country’s age structure.

label: Women & girls
question: Which country has a larger share of women and girls?
definition: Female residents as a share of the total population, using the source’s population estimates. Includes girls as well as adults and counts residents regardless of citizenship.

label: Size of the economy
question: Which country has the larger economy?
definition: Total annual economic output, measured as GDP in current US dollars at market exchange rates. This is the size of the whole economy, not output per person, household wealth, or purchasing-power-adjusted GDP.

label: Economic growth
question: Which country has a higher economic growth rate?
definition: Annual growth in real GDP: total economic output adjusted for price changes. Negative values mean the economy contracted. This measures growth during the stated year, not the size of the economy.

label: Inflation
question: Which country has a higher inflation rate?
definition: Annual change in the consumer price index, based on a basket of goods and services. This measures how fast prices changed during the stated year, not which country is more expensive. Negative values mean average consumer prices fell.

label: Unemployment
question: Which country has a higher unemployment rate?
definition: People without work who are available for and seeking employment, as a share of the labor force. People not seeking work are outside this denominator. Uses modeled ILO estimates.

label: Women in the workforce
question: Where does a larger share of women work or look for work?
definition: Women aged 15 or over who are employed or unemployed and actively participating in the labor force, as a share of all women in that age group. Uses modeled ILO estimates; this is not the share of workers who are women.

label: Military spending
question: Which country spends a larger share of its economy on the military?
definition: Military expenditure as a percentage of GDP, using SIPRI’s estimates. Includes military personnel, operations, procurement, and military research. This is a share of the economy, not the share of the government budget.

label: Research & development
question: Which country spends a larger share of its economy on research?
definition: Domestic spending on research and development as a share of GDP. Includes businesses, government, universities, and private nonprofits, and covers basic research, applied research, and experimental development.

label: Researchers
question: Which country has more researchers per person?
definition: Researchers engaged in research and development per million residents, measured in full-time-equivalent roles. Includes relevant postgraduate researchers. This measures time spent doing research, not a headcount of everyone with a science degree.

label: Scientific publications
question: Which country produces more scientific papers per person?
definition: Science and engineering journal articles and conference papers indexed by Scopus, divided by the same country’s population in the same year. International coauthors split publication credit between countries. Coverage is not every paper or every academic field.

label: Education spending
question: Which country puts a larger share of its economy into public education?
definition: Government expenditure on education as a share of GDP, including current spending, capital spending, and transfers. Covers local, regional, and central government. Private household spending is not included.

label: Healthcare spending
question: Which country spends a larger share of its economy on healthcare?
definition: Current spending on healthcare goods and services as a share of GDP, including public and private spending. Excludes capital investments such as hospital buildings and major equipment. Higher spending does not by itself measure better care.

label: Doctors
question: Which country has more doctors per person?
definition: Generalist and specialist medical practitioners per 1,000 residents. Reporting and training definitions vary between countries. This national average does not show how evenly doctors are distributed within the country.

label: Hospital beds
question: Which country has more hospital beds per person?
definition: Inpatient beds in public, private, general, and specialized hospitals and rehabilitation centers, per 1,000 residents. Usually includes both acute and chronic care. Bed counts do not measure the quality or availability of treatment.

label: Landline subscriptions
question: Which country has more landline subscriptions per person?
definition: Fixed telephone subscriptions per 100 residents, including conventional lines, fixed VoIP services, and public payphones. Includes homes and organizations; it does not count unique people or mobile subscriptions.

label: Safe drinking water
question: Where does a larger share of people have safe drinking water?
definition: People using an improved drinking-water source that is on their premises, available when needed, and free from fecal and priority chemical contamination. The measure requires all three conditions, not just a piped connection.

label: Sanitation
question: Where does a larger share of people have basic sanitation at home?
definition: People using improved sanitation facilities that are not shared with other households. Includes flush toilets, suitable pit latrines, and composting toilets, as well as safely managed sanitation. Shared facilities do not qualify as basic under this measure.
